analysis.title: Landlords Win, Middlemen Lose, & The Fed Can't Look Through Anything: Goldman's Top 10 Charts
key_insights: Goldman's Chryssafis ranks the week's cross-asset movers by standardized weekly range. Winners were USD vs oil exporters and safe havens (USDCAD +2.63, USDNOK +1.93, USDCHF +1.68). Losers were CCC high yield (-2.86), 2Y Treasury futures (-2.05) and 5Y (-1.80).

Goldman names three cross-currents for risk markets: the AI hardware/infrastructure debate after the midterms, weak energy prices, and a hotter than expected CPI pressuring the Fed for more and faster hikes. Traders are boosting bets on a 50bp hike in December.

Goldman view on AI: hyperscalers that control existing power and computing capacity gain leverage as new supply becomes harder to build. Independent model developers and cloud intermediaries depend on access to that infrastructure.
Goldman put 45% of planned US data center capacity in the moratorium crosshairs after the Democratic sweep. Hyperscalers rallied and builders sold off the day after the vote.

IG hyperscaler spread has widened to roughly 163bps from about 100bps earlier in the year, almost 50bps wide of the 30Y IG index (115bps). Being well positioned does not make hyperscalers cheap to finance in credit.

Neocloud complex is more exposed. Per Chamath Palihapitiya's framework in Goldman's Top of Mind, operators that own land, power and shell have leverage, while lease-only operators are middlemen with a business model that requires operational perfection.

CoreWeave CDS has more than doubled since May, from roughly 530bps to 1,142bps, after peaking near 1,300bps in early November. Its 9.75% 2031 bonds yield roughly 15%. The company guided to a $1.1B quarterly interest bill with debt at $47B.
Goldman's head of leveraged finance says non-IG AI supply has dried up, with no new deals in the past month after roughly 30 over the prior year.

Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO, President and director effective immediately. CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO. The stock fell 10% to its lowest since July 2025. Goldman says NVDA pain may compound pressure on neoclouds (NVDA seen as the 'central bank of AI').

Goldman's Jim Schneider uses Apple around Steve Jobs' 2011 leave and death as the analog: Apple de-rated from ~17X to ~12X NTM P/E over ~18 months, hit ~9X in 2013, then recovered to ~15X. Goldman sees NVDA's current price as favorable risk/reward given ~80% expected EPS growth. Next earnings are Nov 17 with Kress delivering.

A NY Times poll of Texas and Ohio voters showed AI/data centers at about 1% or less as the most important issue, while the economy topped the list. Goldman says the economy and the AI buildout are closely linked.

Goldman economists estimate wealth effects added more than 0.4pp to annualized consumption growth in 2026. In a downside case (AI stocks down 30%, everything else down 15%), the effect swings to roughly a 0.6pp drag on real PCE growth by late 2027.

Goldman added a third 25bp hike to its forecast, penciled in for March 2027, expecting most FOMC participants to signal it in the December dot plot. Terminal rate forecast is unchanged at 3.25-3.5%, still reached via later cuts.
Goldman scenario weights: 35% chance of four hikes and a higher terminal rate, 15% for recession. Market pricing sits above Goldman's baseline and probability-weighted path out to 2028.

Goldman says Trump's post reinforces the Iran blockade. The next political milestone is the Dec 11 government spending deadline. Kalshi puts shutdown odds on Dec 12 at 38%, down 8 points, ranging 30-45% for weeks.

Praneet Shah's chart maps assets by sensitivity to an AI rebound and a US 2Y policy shock. The 'Dovish Goldilocks' quadrant holds NDX, SOX, Russell 2000, Korea and Taiwan equities, TWD, ILS and AUD. Chryssafis says it can be unlocked if the conflict stops constraining the Fed, with dispersion favoring pristine balance sheets.

market_movers.rationale: Schneider says the stock price likely represents favorable risk/reward given ~80% expected EPS growth, despite the CEO resignation and a likely multiple de-rating.

Lease-only operators are middlemen dependent on infrastructure access, with CDS above 1,100bps and the junk market shut.

earnings_insights: NVDA reports earnings Nov 17 (upcoming, not yet printed), the first test after the CEO resignation, delivered by interim CEO Kress. Goldman expects ~80% EPS growth (estimate).
CoreWeave's latest reported quarter guided to a $1.1 billion quarterly interest bill, with debt at $47 billion, and did not blow up.

tension_points.bull_case: Bond bulls argue the FOMC should look through hot CPI prints because energy prices are falling.
tension_points.bear_case: Goldman says further Middle East escalation or no resolution may handicap the Fed's ability to look through, and it added a third hike for March 2027.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A resolution of the Iran conflict and a cooperative January inflation report would unlock the Dovish Goldilocks quadrant.

tension_points.bull_case: ~80% expected EPS growth can outrun the leadership discount, as with Apple after Jobs when price rose through most of the de-rating.
tension_points.bear_case: Apple's NTM P/E fell from ~17X to ~12X and as low as ~9X in 2013 before recovering to ~15X.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Nov 17 earnings delivered by interim CEO Kress are the first test of the bull case.
